problem: Prior robot spatio-temporal memory and video-QA systems only handle short histories (about 30 s to 2 min). Long-context approaches such as MobilityVLA put an entire tour into a 1M-token Gemini context, which cannot scale to unbounded, ever-growing deployment histories. EQA-style systems also give text-only answers that a navigation robot cannot act on.
motivation: Robots are deployed for hours in the same place and see static objects, dynamic events and signs that metric or semantic maps do not capture. Users want to ask where, when, how long ago, or whether something happened. The key observation is that any single question needs only a small subset R of the full history H, so a retrieval-based memory can replace putting the whole history in context.
key_idea: Continuously caption short video segments with a VLM and store caption embeddings with position and timestamp in a vector database; at query time, an LLM agent iteratively issues text, position and time retrieval calls and returns structured, actionable answers (xy position, time, duration, or text).
insight:
Framing long-horizon memory as retrieval over time- and position-tagged caption memories keeps answer latency roughly constant as history grows, and it beats feeding all captions or frames to GPT-4o on medium and long videos. Ablations (Table 2) show what matters:
- Iterative multi-step retrieval: a single call drops overall correctness from 0.72/0.56/0.61 to 0.67/0.48/0.50.
- Fine caption granularity: 12-second instead of 3-second captions drops Long correctness to 0.38.
- Captioner size matters less: VILA1.5-3b gives 0.60/0.58/0.50.
- The LLM matters most: open-source LLMs can form the function calls but fail at the spatial and temporal arithmetic, with position errors above 150 m.
method: Memory building: VILA1.5-13b captions each 3-s video segment (6 frames, about 2 FPS) from the front camera, captions are embedded with mxbai-embed-large-v1, and each caption embedding is stored in a vector database with its position (GPS/odometry) and timestamp.
Problem decomposition: approximate p(A|H,Q) by p(A|R,Q), where R is a minimal subset of the history sampled from the memory V by an LLM agent acting as the sampling function F.

LLM-agent retrieval loop: a state-machine LLM generates up to k queries per iteration, using text retrieval f_l(object), position retrieval f_p((x,y,z)) or time retrieval f_t('HH:MM:SS'); each query returns m memories (caption, position, time).
Answerability check: after each iteration the LLM decides whether the question is answerable; if not, it re-queries (up to 3 retrieval steps); if so, it summarizes the relevant memories and answers.
Structured output: the answer is JSON with text, position, time or duration keys, so it can be evaluated directly and used as a metric navigation goal.

Robot deployment: quantized VILA-3b, Whisper ASR, the vector DB and the ROS2 Nav2 stack (AMCL on a pre-mapped map, 3D LiDAR) run on a Jetson Orin 32GB on a Nova Carter robot, with GPT-4o as the agent backend.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) LLM agent; also Codestral, Command-R, Llama3.1-8B; VILA1.5-13b captioner (VILA-3b quantized on robot) + mxbai-embed-large-v1 text embedder (all frozen)
setting.model_size: GPT-4o (undisclosed) agent + 13B captioner (3B/8B captioners ablated); Llama3.1 variant is 8B
setting.training_data: none (training-free); evaluated on the new NaVQA dataset (210 questions on 7 CODa sequences)
setting.observation: front-facing monocular RGB video + GPS/localized position + timestamps (history accumulated over deployment)
setting.action_space: outputs a metric (x,y,z) goal position / time / duration / text answer; on the robot the goal is executed by the Nav2 planner
setting.simulator: none (offline CODa real-robot videos) + real world
setting.privileged: robot localization assumed (GPS in CODa; AMCL on a pre-built metric map in deployment); the memory is built from the robot's own prior traversal, which is the task input

numbers.extra: up to 3 retrieval steps; 3-s captions; averaged over 3 seeds (baselines 1 seed); temporal error column labelled (s) in paper

numbers_note:
NaVQA has no official splits; the 210 questions are grouped into Short (<2 min), Medium (2-7 min) and Long (>7 min) videos, encoded as metric suffixes. Accuracy and overall correctness are printed as 0-1 values in the paper and converted to 0-100 here. Temporal error is labelled '(s)' in Table 1, but the values (0.3-18.7) and the 2-minute correctness threshold suggest minutes; the numbers are copied as printed. Overall correctness is reported only for the GPT-4o ReMEmbR and its ablations; baseline overall correctness over time appears only in Figure 4. The Multi-Frame VLM baseline could not process Medium/Long videos. Further Table 2 overall-correctness ablations (Short/Medium/Long, not listed as entries):
- 1 call only: 0.67/0.48/0.50
- 12-sec captions: 0.54/0.50/0.38
- Llama-VILA1.5-8b captioner: 0.58/0.52/0.54
- VILA1.5-3b captioner: 0.60/0.58/0.50
results: On NaVQA, ReMEmbR with GPT-4o beats GPT-4o given all captions at once on Long videos: 0.65 vs 0.55 descriptive accuracy, 46.25 m vs 56.0 m position error, and 3.6 vs 8.0 temporal error. It matches the multi-frame GPT-4o VLM on Short videos (position error 5.1 m vs 7.5 m), and that VLM cannot process Medium/Long videos at all. Overall correctness is 0.72/0.56/0.61 (Short/Medium/Long). Latency stays about 25 s per question for a 21.5-min video, versus about 90 s for the VLM on a 5.5-min video. Open-source LLM backends perform far worse, with position errors of about 150-210 m.
limitations: Memory relies solely on video captions: it misses richer spatial structure (room labels, scene graphs, semantic maps), and caption errors from a small quantized captioner cause wrong goals (e.g., a water fountain captioned as a 'silver machine' was taken for a soda machine).
The vector DB keeps adding repetitive memories that dilute useful information over time; there is no memory consolidation.
Small evaluation: 210 questions on 7 CODa sequences with unique answers only; baselines run with 1 seed; real-robot results are qualitative only.
